chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Aban ibn Uthman from one who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a mukatab (a slave who has been manumitted upon payment of a fixed sum) who was bequeathed a legacy, and he has paid what he was obligated to pay except for a small amount, he said: 'It is permissible [to deduct the legacy] proportionally to what is freed from him [the remaining debt].'

key_terms.مَا أُعْتِقَ مِنْهُ: What is freed from him (referring to the portion of the debt paid).
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.

ai.seo_question: How is a legacy handled for a slave who still owes part of his manumission price?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of proportional deduction is applied to facilitate the emancipation of a mukatab, ensuring that any bequest left to him is offset against his outstanding manumission debt. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on easing the burden of slaves toward freedom, balancing the rights of the master with the beneficiary's entitlement. The ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic inheritance law when dealing with conditional freedom contracts.
